gloss: to get on track; to get going smoothly

definitions.gloss: to get on track; to get into full swing; to start running smoothly
definitions.explanation: Used when a project, business, plan, or activity passes its initial difficulties and begins to operate steadily and successfully.

examples.japanese: {事業|じぎょう}が{軌道|きどう}に{乗|の}った。
{計画|けいかく}がやっと{軌道|きどう}に{乗|の}り{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: The plan is finally starting to get on track.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{生活|せいかつ}が{軌道|きどう}に{乗|の}るまでに{半年|はんとし}かかった。
examples.english: It took half a year for my new life to get into a steady rhythm.

examples.japanese: {開店|かいてん}から{三|さん}ヶ{月|げつ}で{経営|けいえい}が{軌道|きどう}に{乗|の}り、{黒字|くろじ}になった。
examples.english: Three months after opening, the management got on track and turned profitable.

notes:
Literally 'to ride on a track/orbit.' The metaphor compares a smoothly running operation to a train on its tracks or a satellite in orbit. Very commonly used in business and project contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {事業|じぎょう}が{軌道|きどう}に{乗|の}る: the business gets on track
- {経営|けいえい}が{軌道|きどう}に{乗|の}る: management gets on track
- {計画|けいかく}が{軌道|きどう}に{乗|の}る: the plan gets on track
- {生活|せいかつ}が{軌道|きどう}に{乗|の}る: life settles into a routine
- {軌道|きどう}に{乗|の}せる: to put on track (transitive form)

USAGE:
The transitive counterpart {軌道|きどう}に{乗|の}せる means 'to put something on track' — i.e., to make a project start running smoothly through one's efforts.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {順調|じゅんちょう}に{進|すす}む: to proceed smoothly — describes ongoing smooth progress, while {軌道|きどう}に{乗|の}る marks the transition from struggle to stability
- {波|なみ}に{乗|の}る: to ride a wave; to get into a groove — more casual, emphasizes momentum
